key_insight: The paper introduces a phase diagram that explains when cross-modal alignment (CA) or cross-modal prediction (CP) is the better choice for multimodal learning. It shows that cross-modal training is not universally beneficial; its success depends on the data regime and the relationship between modalities.
problem_solved: It addresses the lack of a systematic framework for understanding when multimodal methods help, when they fail, and whether alignment or prediction is the right objective. This is especially important for complex scientific settings with heterogeneous sensors, scales, and measurements.
method: Build a phase-diagram-style analysis of multimodal learning regimes.
Compare cross-modal alignment and cross-modal prediction across different data conditions.
Identify when cross-modal training improves representation learning versus when it can be ineffective or harmful.
impact: This gives practitioners a practical diagnostic tool for choosing multimodal objectives instead of relying on one-size-fits-all methods. It can improve model design in domains like biomedicine and astrophysics, where modality relationships are complex and standard approaches often underperform.
visual_elements: A two-axis phase diagram showing regions where CA or CP works best
A side-by-side comparison panel of alignment vs prediction
Icons representing heterogeneous modalities such as imaging, signals, and text
A flowchart for selecting the right multimodal strategy based on data regime
paper_title: When to Align, When to Predict: A Phase Diagram for Multimodal Learning
paper_authors: Ilay Kamai, Hugues Van Assel, Aviv Regev, Hagai B. Perets, Randall Balestriero
